surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Flames get past the Hurricanes
paras: The second period was a wild one. Jesperi Kotkaniemi got the scoring started for the Hurricanes early in the period. Matvei Gridin and Morgan Frost scored just over a minute apart late in the period to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead. Jalen Chatfield tied it 2-2 for Carolina with just four seconds left in the period, but that was the last goal the Hurricanes would get. Yegor Sharangovich put the Flames ahead for good with four and a half minutes left.

The Hurricanes had a little more of the play and hit four posts and the crossbar, but the Flames made their chances count. Devin Cooley, who gave up seven goals against Colorado in his last start, made 34 saves for the Flames, and Brandon Bussi stopped 31 of 34 at the other end. The Flames improved to 2-6-0 and climbed out of last place in the NHL, while the Canes fell to 7-2-1, slipping out of first in the NHL.

items.text: The Hurricanes’ seven-game heater is over.
Jaccob Slavin passed Andrew Cassels for ninth on the Hurricanes’ all-time assists list, with 254.
Jalen Chatfield scored his first goal of the season, his first since Mar 22 (18 games played since).
Mark Jankowski was in NHL.com’s projected lineup, but Nicolas Deslauriers played instead.
